- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted peak by 3–5% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), smooth forecast transitions to avoid erratic overshoots.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to prevent lagged overestimation.
- If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3), shift forecast downward 1–3% to reflect sentiment shift.
- Don’t forecast beyond 10% above recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.85) and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
